result.title: SlotAVS: Object-Centric Audio-Visual Segmentation via Bi-Modal Slot Attention
result.summary: Audio-Visual Segmentation (AVS) requires predicting pixel-wise masks of sounding objects by grounding acoustic signals in visual space. In multi-source scenes, concurrent sound sources often remain entangled within shared visual representations, leading to merged masks or unstable specialization when using standard alignment-focused transformer architectures. To address this, we present SlotAVS, an object-centric framework driven by competitive bi-modal slot attention. While robust foundation models provide rich semantic priors, SlotAVS shifts the paradigm from global cross-modal fusion to explicit competitive binding. By initializing discrete object slots from temporal audio sequences and enforcing strict slot-wise competition over spatial visual tokens, our method structurally mitigates the blending of distinct acoustic entities. Further, to stabilize instance-level learning, we introduce a Hungarian matching strategy that optimally aligns slots with ground-truth objects using spatial and boundary overlap. Coupled with a numerically stable, confidence-aware mask fusion mechanism, SlotAVS robustly aggregates multi-source predictions. Extensive experiments on the AVSBench dataset demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, achieving 88.6% mIoU on the Single-Source (S4) split and 71.7% mIoU on the Multi-Source (MS3) split. These results show that explicit competitive binding is critical for complex audio-visual scene understanding and effectively leveraging foundation-model priors without relying solely on their capacity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SlotAVS，用双模态 slot attention 从音频时序初始化离散物体槽，并在视觉 token 上施加严格的槽间竞争绑定，配合匈牙利匹配与置信度感知掩码融合，在 AVSBench 上完成多声源音视频目标分割（S4 88.6%、MS3 71.7% mIoU）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其离散槽位竞争绑定与匈牙利匹配可能为 LVR 中实体级内部状态的组织、视觉证据筛选与贡献分配提供方法线索，但该工作是像素级感知分割而非多模态推理，需核查槽表示能否迁移到 latent 推理状态。
